key_cases.case_name: People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals, Inc. v. Department of Agricultural Resources
key_cases.holding: The SJC construed the public safety and privacy exemptions to the public records law, holding that the statutes favor disclosure by presuming records are public and placing on the custodian the burden of proving with specificity that an exemption applies.
key_cases.relevance: PETA is the SJC's framework for obtaining the financial and programmatic records that audits depend on.
key_cases.quote: Together, these statutes, and our cases interpreting them, favor disclosure of public records in two primary ways.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court reversed, holding that the "reasonable efforts" clause of the Adoption Assistance and Child Welfare Act of 1980 confers no federally enforceable right on the children it benefits and creates no implied private cause of action, leaving compliance to be enforced by the Secretary of Health and Human Services through the state-plan approval and funding process.
key_cases.relevance: Suter is the controlling federal authority locating child-welfare funding compliance in the Secretary's plan-approval and audit powers, the legal foundation of OIG and Single Audit Act review; no Massachusetts or First Circuit decision on those programs was located.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the Act does not create an enforceable right on behalf of respondents.
